mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 2.5% over the next month reduces discount rates applied to corporate cash flows, lowering the present value of future earnings and thus producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the following 20-day period.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises continuously for 4 consecutive months above 2.5%
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive or flat during the identified rising rate period, or the IC is not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05) in a 3-month rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strong labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and equity valuations, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by > 5,000 in a month while UNRATE falls by > 0.2 percentage points
failure_condition: No significant correlation between PAYEMS and UNRATE changes (Pearson IC < 0.2), or 60-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in household spending proxies (HOUST) exceeding 3% suggests accelerating consumer demand, which elevates earnings expectations and supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: Over 40% of triggered months show non-positive 5-day forward returns, or IC < -0.1 in a 10-day rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) accompanied by a decline in inflation (CPIAUCSL) indicates supply-side constraints, raising uncertainty and pushing down equity valuations, which predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by > 2% in a month while CPIAUCSL decreases by > 0.5%
failure_condition: No significant interaction detected (IC < 0.15), or 20-day forward returns are not statistically negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate remains below 1.5% for three consecutive months during a financial market stress episode, lower borrowing costs encourage leveraged investors to increase equity exposure, producing positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 1.5% for 3 consecutive months and VIX > 20 over the same period
failure_condition: IC between FEDFUNDS and 20-day returns is not significant (p > 0.05), or returns are not positive in > 60% of such episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden one-standard-deviation increase in monthly job openings (PAYEMS) without a corresponding rise in unemployment suggests a tight labor market, which can fuel wage growth and equity risk appetite, leading to positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by at least one standard deviation above its 12-month mean in a single month
failure_condition: No positive 60-day returns in 80% of such events, or unemployment rate does not decline in response (IC < 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of declining industrial production (INDPRO) coupled with rising inflation (CPIAUCSL) indicate weakening supply chains and cost pressures, which typically precede equity market volatility and negative 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls for 3 consecutive months while CPIAUCSL increases by > 0.3%
failure_condition: No significant interaction (IC < 0.2), or 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of steadily declining consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL), the S&P 500 tends to exhibit positive 5-day forward returns as the market anticipates the Federal Reserve holding rates steady, reducing the risk of a sharp tightening cycle.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL decreases continuously for 4 months while FEDFUNDS remains unchanged
failure_condition: Over 70% of such episodes produce non-positive 5-day returns, or IC between CPIAUCSL and returns is negative (p < 0.05).
